messages:
Ria (support): FYI - support got a P1 from a customer seeing repeated 429s + high tail latency during a short traffic spike. They call it a '5-minute storm' with multiple API keys.
Sam (eng-platform): Can you paste the repro steps / any request patterns?
Ria (support): Customer says: sudden surge over ~90s, roughly 30k requests, ~4 keys, each key ~7-9 concurrent clients. Observed errors: 429 rate_exceeded, occasional 502/503 during the peak. They sent a short log: 
```
2026-03-14T18:22:11Z request_id=tr-9a1e status=200 latency_ms=120
2026-03-14T18:22:12Z request_id=tr-9a1f status=429 error=rate_exceeded
2026-03-14T18:22:13Z request_id=tr-9a20 status=503 error=backend_timeout
```
Sam (eng-platform): Thanks. Sounds like multi-key burst exhaustion + some downstream queueing/coldstart noise. Can we run a targeted loadlab run to reproduce locally? Suggested pattern: keyed spike (many keys, short burst windows).
Zoe (eng-sre): I'll spin up the lab. Proposed params: 8 keys, duration 10m, per-key RPS ramp to 25 for 90s, global token pressure to hit TPM ~60k. Command: 
```
loadlab run --pattern keyed-spike --keys 8 --rps-per-key 25 --burst-window 90 --duration 600 --trace true
```
Mike (eng-infra): Important to include header `X-Client-Id` per-key and enable sampling for `request_trace_id`. Also capture `quota.bucket` metrics and token refill logs.
loadlab-bot: starting run 2101234567-01, cluster=staging-loadlab, injector=10. ETA ~2m.
Ria (support): While we wait, any hypothesis on sane defaults we should recommend to support for RPM/TPM and burst behavior? Customer likely needs guidance to avoid saturation.
Sam (eng-platform): Quick heuristics we use internally: per-key sustained RPM = 600 (10 RPS) for general accounts, burst allowance = 2x sustained for a short window (60–120s) but with leaky-bucket smoothing. TPM (tokens/min) depends on average token size; for chat workloads default TPM=100k with burst headroom to 200k.
Zoe (eng-sre): From earlier experiments, multi-key spikes tend to break shared pools. Add guardrails: per-key concurrency cap (e.g., 50 inflight), global soft-queue limit, and prefer per-org aggregated limits rather than naive sum of per-key bursts. Also enforce cooldown: if 429s persist >30s, reduce burst multiplier to 1.
Mike (eng-infra): For default rate-window math we recommend: window=60s, refill_rate = sustained_RPM/60, bucket_capacity = sustained_RPM * burst_multiplier. Example: sustained_RPM=600 => refill=10/s, capacity=1200 if burst_multiplier=2 (so immediate allowance up to 1200 requests).
loadlab-bot: run complete. Summary: sustained RPS baseline ok, spike produced 429s at ~75s, throttles hit per-key bucket_capacity, backend latency spiked to 800-1200ms correlated with queue depth. Traces: sample trace tr-9a20 shows retry storm and token_cache_miss.
Sam (eng-platform): Repro confirmed. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) tune defaults (per-key RPM 600, burst multiplier 1.5–2, burst-window 60s) 2) improve smoothing + early-fail responses (provide Retry-After and rapid-fail clients to backoff).
Ria (support): I'll propose messaging: "We throttle to protect customers during sudden spikes. Recommended per-key sustained RPM 600, short bursts allowed up to 1200 RPM/window (60s). If you expect consistent higher spikes, request dedicated capacity."
Zoe (eng-sre): Also add a runbook entry: how to reproduce with `loadlab`, which metrics to attach, and what to check in traces (bucket refill, kv-cache misses, model coldstart events).
Mike (eng-infra): Action items: (1) eng-platform to update rate-default doc + sample config, (2) SRE to add a dashboard for burst saturation (bucket_utilization, queue_depth), (3) Support to use the new repro command in initial triage.
Ria (support): Sounds good — I'll draft the reply to the customer with the suggested defaults and ask if they can share spike traces. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sam (eng-platform): I'll open a tiny PR to docs with the math examples and the `loadlab` snippet. Assign to Mike for infra instrumentation follow-up.
Zoe (eng-sre): Leaving notes in the incident tracker: INC-2026-2143.
Ria (support): Closing loop here, will re-open if customer still sees issues after guidance.
